title: Celsus on abstaining from sacrificial meat
source_text: Ἐκθέμενοι δὲ καὶ τὴν ἑξῆς λέξιν φέρε πάλιν κατὰ δύναμιν αὐτὴν ἐξετάσωμεν οὕτως ἔχουσαν· εἰ μὲν δὴ κατά τι πάτριον ἱερείων τινῶν ἀπέχονται τῶν τοιῶνδε, πάντως ἀφεκτέον καὶ ζῴων ἁπάντων βρώσεως· ᾗ περ καὶ Πυθαγόρᾳ δοκεῖ, ψυχὴν τιμῶντι καὶ τὰ ταύτης ὄργανα. εἰ δ᾿. ὅπερ φασὶν, ὅπως μὴ συνεστιῶνται δαίμοσι. μακαρίζω τῆς σοφίας αὐτοὺς. ὅτι βραδέως συνιᾶσιν ὄντες ἀεὶ συνέστιοι δαιμόνων· καὶ τότε δὴ μόνον φυλάσσονται τοῦτο, ὁπόταν ἱερεῖον θυόμενον βλέπωσιν· ὅταν δὲ σῖτον ἐσθίωσι καὶ οἶνον πίνωσι καὶ ἀκροδρύων γεύωνται καὶ αὐτὸ ὕδωρ καὶ αὐτὸν ἀέρα ἀναπνέωσιν, οὐκ ἄρα παρά τινων δαιμόνων ἕκαστα τούτων λαμβάνουσιν, οἷς κατὰ μέρη τὸ ἐπιμελὲς ἑκάστῳ προστέτακται; οὐκ οἶδ᾿ ὅπως ἐν τούτοις ἔδοξεν αὐτῷ ἀκολουθεῖν δεῖν ἀπέχεσθαι πάντων ζῴων βρώσεως τοὺς, οὓς ὠνόμασε κατά τι πάτριον ἔθος ἱερείων τινῶν ἀπεχομένους. καὶ οὐ τοῦτό φαμεν, ὡς καὶ μὴ τοιαῦτα ὑποβάλλοντος τοῦ θείου λόγου, καὶ τοῦ ἀσφαλεστέρου βίου καὶ καθαρωτέρου ἕνεκεν εἰπόντος· „καλὸν τὸ μὴ φαγεῖν κρέα μηδὲ πιεῖν οἶνον μηδὲ ἐν ᾧ ὁ ἀδελφός σου προσκόπτει“ καὶ πάλιν· „μὴ τῷ βρώματί σου ἐκεῖνον ἀπόλλυε, ὑπὲρ οὗ Χριστὸς ἀπέθανε,“ καὶ πάλιν· „εἰ σκανδαλίζει τὸν ἀδελφόν μου κρέα, οὐ μὴ φάγω κρέα εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ἵνα μὴ τὸν ἀδελφόν μου σκανδαλίσω.“
pass_a_gloss: Having set out (ἐκτίθημι) also the next passage (λέξις), come (φέρε), again let us examine (ἐξετάζω) it according to ability (κατὰ δύναμιν), being thus: [Celsus] if indeed according to some ancestral (πάτριος) [custom] they abstain (ἀπέχομαι) from certain such victims (ἱερεῖον), entirely (πάντως) one must abstain (ἀφεκτέον) also from eating (βρῶσις) all living creatures (ζῷον), as also seems [right] to Pythagoras, honouring (τιμάω) soul (ψυχή) and its instruments/organs (ὄργανον). But if, as they say, so that they may not feast together (συνεστιάομαι) with demons (δαίμων), I congratulate (μακαρίζω) them on their wisdom (σοφία), that slowly (βραδέως) they understand (συνίημι) being always table-companions (συνέστιος) of demons; and then only guard against (φυλάσσομαι) this, whenever they see a victim being sacrificed (θύω); but when they eat bread/grain (σῖτος) and drink wine (οἶνος) and taste fruits (ἀκρόδρυα) and [take] water itself and breathe (ἀναπνέω) air itself (ἀήρ), do they not then receive each of these from certain demons, to whom by parts (κατὰ μέρη) the care (τὸ ἐπιμελές) has been assigned (προστάσσω) to each? [Origen] I do not know how in these [words] it seemed to him to follow (ἀκολουθεῖν) that those must abstain from eating all living creatures whom he named as abstaining from certain victims by some ancestral custom (ἔθος). And we do not say this as though the divine word (θεῖος λόγος) did not also suggest (ὑποβάλλω) such things, and, for the sake of a safer (ἀσφαλής) and purer (καθαρός) life (βίος), said: 'good not to eat meat (κρέας) nor drink wine nor [anything] in which your brother stumbles (προσκόπτω)'; and again 'do not by your food (βρῶμα) destroy (ἀπόλλυμι) that one for whom Christ died'; and again 'if meat causes my brother to stumble (σκανδαλίζω), I will not eat meat ever (εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα), so that I may not cause my brother to stumble.'
pass_b_english: Let us set out the next passage as well, and once again examine it as best we can. It runs as follows: “If, by some ancestral custom, they abstain from certain sacrificial victims of this kind, then they must surely abstain from eating any animal at all, as Pythagoras too thinks, who honours the soul and its instruments. But if, as they say, it is so that they may not feast with demons, I congratulate them on their wisdom, that they are slow to see that they are always the table-companions of demons. They guard against this only when they see a victim being sacrificed. But when they eat bread and drink wine and taste fruits, and drink even water itself and breathe the very air, do they not receive each of these from certain demons, to each of whom the care of his own share has been assigned?”

I do not know how he came to think it follows from this that those whom he described as abstaining from certain victims by some ancestral custom must abstain from eating any animal at all. And we do not say this as though the divine word did not also counsel such things, and did not say, for the sake of a safer and purer life: “It is good not to eat meat or drink wine or do anything by which your brother stumbles” (Romans 14:21); and again: “Do not by your food destroy the one for whom Christ died” (Romans 14:15); and again: “If meat makes my brother stumble, I will never eat meat, so that I may not make my brother stumble” (1 Corinthians 8:13).

choices.choice: The quotation from Celsus runs from ‘If, by some ancestral custom’ to ‘has been assigned’; Origen’s reply begins ‘I do not know how’. In Celsus’s last question the Greek joins ‘water itself and the air itself’ to the one verb ‘breathe’ (ἀναπνέωσιν); the reviewer supplied ‘drink’ for the water (replacing the first draft’s ‘take’), since in 8.31 Origen restates this clause with ‘the drinker’ (τὸν πίνοντα). ‘Instruments’ (ὄργανα) means the bodies the soul uses; Pythagoras is said to honour the soul in animals and their bodies. In ‘ὡς καὶ μὴ τοιαῦτα ὑποβάλλοντος ... καὶ ... εἰπόντος’ the one negative governs both participles, so both are kept under ‘as though ... did not’. All three Pauline quotations match the received New Testament wording closely; in 1 Corinthians 8:13 Origen has κρέα where Paul has βρῶμα; Romans 14:21 has ‘do anything’ supplied in English for the elliptical μηδὲ ἐν ᾧ. The punctuation of the staged Perseus text has full stops where commas belong; I followed the sense.
'certain such sacrificial victims' smoothed to 'certain sacrificial victims of this kind'
'even take water itself' corrected to 'drink even water itself' (zeugma; Origen's restatement in 8.31 has 'the drinker')
restored the negative scope over both participles: 'as though the divine word did not also counsel such things, and did not say ...' (draft turned the second into a positive assertion)
translator note updated for the water verb, negation scope and κρέα/βρῶμα in 1 Corinthians 8:13
